subject.title: [Feature]: Outbound Task Calls — Agent makes phone calls on user's behalf (reservations, inquiries, flight changes)

question: What safety and product contract should OpenClaw require before supporting autonomous outbound task calls that speak to third parties and disclose user-authorized information?
rationale: The remaining work crosses consent, disclosure, privacy, retention, provider exposure, cost-control, and long-lived session-state boundaries that cannot be selected safely from code inspection alone.

options.title: Design a plugin-owned task-call contract
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define the Voice Call API, disclosure and allowed-information rules, retention/redaction model, escalation behavior, hold/callback timeouts, and cost limits before implementation.

options.title: Limit scope to external telephony plugins
options.body: Treat OpenClaw core as providing only primitives and ask task-call orchestration to live in a ClawHub/plugin integration unless a missing plugin API is identified.

options.title: Close as not planned
options.body: Reject autonomous third-party calling in OpenClaw if the legal, privacy, provider, or product risks are not worth carrying in the project.

recommendation.title: Design a plugin-owned task-call contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define the Voice Call API, disclosure and allowed-information rules, retention/redaction model, escalation behavior, hold/callback timeouts, and cost limits before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent Voice Call feature/API history and already provided the maintainer-facing keep-open analysis for this umbrella.
